newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian Ukio Bank plans GDR issue.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian Ukio Bank plans GDR issue.

text.p: Lithuanian bank Ukio Bank aims to make an issue of global depository receipts (GDRs) in the second half of this year to boost its capital to 82 million litas from 42 million litas, the bank's chairman said on Monday.

"We want to boost the share capital in the second half of 1997 by quoting GDRs on the Luxembourg bourse but the final decision will be taken by the shareholders meeting," Butenas told Reuters. The shareholders meeting will be in March.
The bank, one of the top five, recently boosted its capital by 18 million litas to 42 million litas and the new shares were bought by Nomura and Swedfund.
More than 50 percent of the bank's shares are now owned by foreigners, Butenas added.
The bank made a five million litas profit during the first nine months of 1996.
"Our strategic direction is the financing of trade, small and medium sized businesses and retail banking," Butenas added.
Lithuanian banks have been gradually recovering from a banking crisis that struck at the end of 1995 and the market has seen the entry of more foreign investors.
Three Lithuanian banks are now more than half-owned by foreigners, with leading banks Vilnius Bank and Hermis Bank also having big foreign shareholders.
